script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. APARTMENT - NIGHT

JAMES (mid-30s, scruffy, worn clothing) sits on his apartment floor surrounded by takeout containers, empty beer bottles, and old newspapers. He looks up as a knock comes from the door.

JAMES
(yelling)
Who is it?

A moment later, the door opens and MICHAEL (mid-30s, neatly dressed) enters, a small smile on his face.

MICHAEL
(cheerfully)
It's me, Michael. I brought dinner.

James groans and pushes himself to his feet.

JAMES
(sarcastically)
Great, another night of my life being saved by you.

Michael sets the bags down on the coffee table and begins unpacking the food.

MICHAEL
(laughs)
You know I enjoy taking care of you.

James sits down on the couch, a pained expression on his face.

JAMES
(sighs)
I just can't seem to get it together these days.

MICHAEL
(sympathetically)
You're going through a rough patch. We all have them. But you'll get through it.

They eat in silence for a moment before James speaks up.

JAMES
(softly)
I don't know what I'd do without you, Michael.

MICHAEL
(smiling)
That's what friends are for, isn't it?

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

James and Michael sit across from each other at a table, sipping coffee. The sun shines through the window, illuminating their faces.

JAMES
(looking thoughtful)
Do you ever wonder what our lives would be like if we hadn't met?

MICHAEL
(grinning)
I've thought about it from time to time. But I wouldn't want to miss out on our friendship.

They share a knowing smile.

JAMES
(serious)
You really mean that?

MICHAEL
(nods)
Absolutely.

INT. JAMES' APARTMENT - NIGHT

James lies in bed, staring at the ceiling. He hears a knock on the door.

JAMES
(weakly)
Come in.

Michael enters, wearing a worried expression.

MICHAEL
(concerned)
What's wrong? You don't sound good.

James turns his head to look at him.

JAMES
(voice cracking)
I've lost my job. I can't pay the rent. I don't know what to do.

Michael sits down on the edge of the bed.

MICHAEL
(calmly)
We'll figure something out. In the meantime, you can stay with me.

James looks up at him, a mix of relief and gratitude in his eyes.

JAMES
(whispers)
Thank you.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

James and Michael sit across from each other, their hands intertwined over the table.

JAMES
(thoughtfully)
I've been thinking a lot about our friendship lately. And I realize that it's the most important thing in my life.

MICHAEL
(smiling)
I feel the same way.

They share a tender moment, their eyes locked on each other.

JAMES
(softly)
I don't know where I'd be without you, Michael.

MICHAEL
(tearfully)
And I wouldn't want to be anywhere else but here with you.

They lean in and share a long, passionate kiss.

INT. JAMES' APARTMENT - NIGHT

James and Michael lie in bed, their bodies entwined.

JAMES
(whispering in Michael's ear)
I love you, Michael.

MICHAEL
(smiling)
I love you too, James.

They fall asleep in each other's arms, their hearts beating in sync.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
